extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical/Euclidean geometry (historical Italian edition/transcription)
extracted.subtask_description: Euclidean-style definitions, propositions and computational rules for squares, quadrilaterals (tetragons), diameters and areas, with worked numerical examples and construction procedures. The text explains how to compute areas, relate squares and roots, and find sides or points by proportional division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: quadrilateral with all right angles
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘campi di 4 facce che' hano tutti gli angoli retti’ — a four‑faced figure whose angles are all right; when opposite sides are equal it forms the rectangle/square cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text explains that when sides are equal and angles right the faces are equal; multiplication of one side by another is used to produce the area (e.g. multiplicatione di lune lato per l'altro è la certa multiplicatione). Examples and reductions follow for specific combinatons of equal/unequal sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: square numbers and simple numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘qiili prodotti ... Dicano quadrati’ — products of a number by itself are called squares; numbers that have no relation to roots or squares are called 'numeri semplici' (simple numbers); composite numbers and their relation to roots are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains terminology: when numbers multiply themselves the root is computed; distinguishes numbers equal to squares, numbers equal to roots, and composite/compound numbers. Provides examples with explicit numbers to illustrate (e.g. 4, 16, 25, relations to their roots).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: multiplication by itself gives square and yields root relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Quando linumeri fi multiplicano in fealora quei numeri fi cicalio radici.’ — when numbers are multiplied by themselves the corresponding square and roots are established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout to move between area (square) and linear measure (root); many worked numeric examples show how to deduce side (root) from square (area) and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: area of square relates to its root (side) and to units
rubrics_metrics.description: If the root of a square is x then the square (area) is x^2; conversely, given area one may take square root to get side. Numerous numeric instances given (e.g. 'la radici del quadrato e ... il quadrato e ... 16 e larea c. 1 6').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples convert between area and side using numbers (cento, 25, 36 etc.), showing the operations of taking roots, halving, multiplying, and reducing to find sides or areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: finding area of specific quadrilaterals (rombi, romboidi, other four‑sided figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text promises methods: 'moƒtraremo il modo a trouare larea cele figure cetre rombi... ilmodo a trouare larea cele figure certe caput abficium… ilmodo a trouare larea cele figure cipm ci.4 lati.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures involve decomposing figures, using known rectangles/squares, multiplying appropriate sides/diagonals, and reducing by subtraction of parts; instructions are illustrated with example figures and algebraic-style manipulations in numerical examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: square on diameter equals double the area of the inscribed tetragon
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘il quadrato Del Diametro e Doppio a larea Del Detto tetragono’ — the square described on the diameter is double the area of the given tetragon (in the specific configuration discussed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim is proved/used with numeric examples: take the area of tetragon, relate it to the square on its diameter, multiply/divide by factors (100, 200, etc.) and take roots to compute sides. Several worked computations show how to reduce or scale to get integral examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure: compute side from area and diameter by multiplication and root extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: To find a side when given the area and a diameter: multiply the area by the diameter (or appropriate power), then take square roots and apply proportion reductions to obtain the linear measure of the side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by numeric sequences (e.g. multiply area by diameter to obtain 100·..., take root yielding side length), with stepwise reductions (divide by 2, take halves, remove multiples) and many numeric examples to follow the arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: relations among multiples/fractions of squares and roots
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about how multiplying the diameter or area by integers affects the resulting squares/roots: e.g. multiplying diameter by 2 produces doubling of certain area relations; multiplying by 10, 100 used as scales to obtain integral roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides many arithmetic identities and worked examples (multiplying by 2, 4, 8, 16, 36, 72 etc.) that show how to scale quantities so that roots are integral or convenient; shows the algebraic effect of such scalings on the area/side relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction technique: dividing a line into equal parts to locate points giving proportional areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeatedly used procedure: divide a line (or diameter) into equal parts and take points (e.g. point b dividing ac in 2 equal parts) such that segments produce areas in desired proportions ('divida in.2 parti iguali fopja il ponto.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to find points whose joined segments cut off sub‑areas equal to given values; text gives constructive sequences for bisecting and partitioning lines to obtain the required proportions and thereby compute side lengths or areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: relations of squares and rectangles built on different sides (comparison of squares on sides/diameters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous equivalences: e.g. 'il quadrato Del lato.bg e il quadrato del lato.ag... il quadrato del diametro ag e doppio al quadrato del lato bg' (comparisons showing how squares on different segments relate by factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to transform problems about one side/segment into another by algebraic identity: adding/subtracting or comparing squares gives method to build required constructions and numeric solving steps; exemplified by many explicit numerical computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compositional rule: assemble areas from component rectangles/squares to obtain target quadrilateral area
rubrics_metrics.description: To find the area of a complex quadrilateral decomposed into rectangles/squares, multiply the appropriate sides/parts and add/subtract component areas ('larea fua fa del multiplicare dela b.in.b c... larea fua e.48').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show partitioning into parts whose areas are known or computable, summing them (or subtracting) to get the whole; the method parallels algebraic addition of squared terms and cross terms to reconstruct areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric exemplification policy: scale by convenient factors (100, 200, 1000, etc.) to avoid fractional roots
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the text the author scales quantities by powers of ten or other convenient integers (100, 200, 1000, 2000, etc.) so that taking roots yields integral or simple results — e.g., 'prendendo la radice di 100 ... la mitta del lato è 2' etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational guideline for practical computation: when raw data give awkward roots, multiply numerator/denominator by suitable squares so the square root becomes rational/integral; many worked examples demonstrate this tactic.
